(Rheumatrex)
Drug inhibits dihydrofolate reductase; decreased 
formation of active folate. Drug may cause GI  
irritation or injury.
All antineoplastic drugs are cytotoxic; potential to 
damage intestinal mucosa.
Drug also used as an antirheumatic.
Maintain diet high in folate and vitamin B12. Daily folic acid supple-
ment may be recommended with antirheumatic doses but is not 
advised with antineoplastic. Leucovorin rescue may be necessary 
with antineoplastic doses. 
Alkylating Agent
•	 cyclophosphamide 
(Cytoxin)
Drug metabolite causes bladder irritation, acute 
hemorrhagic cystitis.
All antineoplastic drugs are cytotoxic; potential to 
damage intestinal mucosa.
Maintain high fluid intake (2-3 L daily) to induce frequent voiding.

Nutritional Implications and Cautions
Epidermal Growth Factor Inhibitor
•	 erlotinib (Tarceva)
Drug may cause anorexia, weight loss, stomatitis, 
nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. Rarely, GI bleeding 
can occur. 
Avoid SJW and grapefruit/related citrus (limes, pomelo, Seville  
oranges). Hold tube feeds 2 hour before and 1 hour after drug.
